A 4670 g (10 lb 5 oz) male newborn was delivered full-term in a 26-year-old woman's womb after a long delivery. The Apgar score is 9 in both minutes 1 and 5. Tests in the delivery room revealed swelling, sensitivity, and crepitus in the left clavicle area. Movement of the left upper limb is reduced. Movement of the hands and wrists is normal. Swallowing reflexes are normal in both hands. An asymmetric Moro reflex is present. The rest of the test has no abnormalities, and enteroposterior X-rays confirm the diagnosis. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?
A. Nerve conductivity test
B. Stabilization by Surgery
C. Physical therapy
D. Adding the pin sleeve to the shirt
E. hand splinting
F. MRI of the clavicle

A 66-year-old male came to the doctor with a three-month history of fatigue. He has high blood pressure and hyperlipidemia. He had suffered a transient ischemic attack (TIA) three years earlier. He drinks 3 beers a day, and sometimes two more at social events. He is currently receiving aspirin, simvastatin, hydrochlorothiazide, and metoprolol. Its temperature is 37.1 ° C (98.8 ° F), pulse is 78, respiration is 19 per minute, and oxygen saturation in room air is 97%. She shows no discomfort but is clearly pale and has multiple fine red, non-blanching spots on her limbs. His spleen is significantly enlarged in palpation. Test results show a hemoglobin of 8.0 g / dL, a white blood cell count of 80,000 / mm3, and a platelet count of 34,000 / mm3. Blood smears show immature cells with large and conspicuous nucleoli and pink, elongated, needle-like cytoplasmic inclusions. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A. Cirrhosis
B. Acute lymphoblastic leukemia
C. Chronic myelogenous leukemia
D. Myelodysplastic syndrome
E. Chronic lymphocytic leukemia
F. Acute myelogenous leukemia

A 40-year-old male patient came to the doctor with five months of watery diarrhea and periodic abdominal crampy pain. She has no fever, nausea, or vomiting. He has lost 1.8 kg (4 lb) in the past six months, although his appetite has not decreased. His wife has noticed that his mouth and throat sometimes turn red after meals or during times of stress. He was diagnosed with asthma a year ago. He is also suffering from high blood pressure. Current medications include albuterol inhalers and enalapril. He drinks a beer every day. Its temperature is 36.7 ° C (98 ° F), pulse 85 / min, blood pressure 130/85 mmHg mercury. It's clear in the lungs. A grade 2 / 6 systolic murmur is heard at the left sternal border and fourth intercostal space. The abdomen is soft, with light tenderness but no guarding or rebound. The rest of the physical exam shows no abnormalities. The complete blood count is within the normal range. If untreated, this patient will be at the highest risk for which of the following conditions?
A. Breath
B. Achlorhydria
C. T-cell lymphoma
D. Megaloblastic anemia
E. Dementia
F. intestinal fistula
G. Arthritis

A 4-year-old boy has been brought to the emergency department because severe abdominal pain and bilious vomiting have been going on for 6 hours. He has not defecated in the last 24 hours. He looks sick. It has a temperature of 37.8 ° C (100 ° F) and a pulse of 122 / min. On examination, the abdomen is swollen. There is pain in the palpation of the lower abdomen; guarding and rebound tenderness are seen. The noise has gone down. An abdominal X-ray shows a hollow intestinal loop. He has a 14-year-old brother. The surgeon recommended an emergency laparotomy. The parents have gone to a friend's house and can't be reached. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?
A. Get consent from the patient's brother
B. Get the patient's consent
C. Collect court orders for surgery
D. Set up a hospital ethics consultation
E. Perform an emergency laparotomy
F. Delay surgery until parental consent is obtained.

A 9-year-old girl was brought to the emergency department, experiencing headaches and double vision an hour after being struck. He was playing with his friend; the friend's elbow struck him just above his left ear and hit his head. He did not lose consciousness, but the mother reported that he was disoriented for 20 minutes after the incident and could not recall being pushed. The patient is recovering well. He is alert and aware of persons, places, and times. His temperature is 37.2 ° C (99 ° F), pulse 86 / min, respiration 15 / min, and blood pressure 118/78 mmHg. Examination shows the head tilted towards the right shoulder. A photo of the eye is shown on the primary gauge. Mild pain is felt by applying gentle pressure on the left temporal bone. Visual acuity 20/20 in both eyes when tested individually. Hypertropia of the patient's left eye increases when looking to the right and when the patient tilts their head to the left shoulder. The pupillae are uniform and reactive to light. Muscle strength and sensation are normal on both sides. The deep tendon reflex is 2 + on both sides, the plantar reflex responds to flexion. Which of the following is the most likely cause of the patient's eye symptoms?
A. Damage to the oculomotor nerve
B. Retrobalbar bleeding
C. Damage to the trochlear nerve
D. Damage to the medial longitudinal fasciculus
E. Dorsal midbrain damage
F. Abdusane nerve damage

A mother takes her 3-year-old son to the pediatrician because he is showing persistent tantrums (excessive anger). The child has no history of serious disease and is on track for developmental milestones. Her mother went back to work two weeks ago. Since then, he said, the boy has done a tantrum almost every other morning, usually when he dresses him up or drops him off at daycare. She cries loudly for about 5 minutes and says she doesn't want to go to the daycare, moving her hands and feet with it. According to the daycare staff, he behaves well throughout the day. In the evenings, there are tantrums about twice a week, usually when he has to finish his meals or say bedtime. These tantrums have been going on for about 6 months. The mother is concerned that her son may have a behavioral disorder. Which of the following is the most likely cause of a child's behavior?
A. Autism spectrum disorder
B. Conduct disorder
C. Normal development
D. Oppositional Defiant Disorder
E. Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder
F. Disruptive mood dysregulation disorder

A 45-year-old male patient came to the doctor with severe left knee pain and swelling. He has hypercholesterolemia and high blood pressure. He is currently receiving pravastatin and captopril. He eats a low-fat diet consisting of fish and leafy vegetables. He drinks 4 to 6 cups of coffee every day. He has been smoking a pack of cigarettes a day for 26 years and drinks 2-3 beers a day. Its vital indicators are within normal limits. Examination of the left knee shows swelling, warmth, and acute sensitivity to touch. Arthrocentesis is performed. Gram stain is negative. Monosodium urate crystals are found in synovial fluid. Which of the following health maintenance recommendations is best suited to prevent the recurrence of symptoms?
A. turn off captopril
B. Start the aspirin.
C. replace beer with red wine
D. Quit smoking
E. Reduce your coffee intake
F. Reduce the amount of fish
G. Stop Provastatin
H. start colchicine

A previously healthy 32-year-old man is brought to the emergency department by his girlfriend, because he has had a seizure (epilepsy). On the same day, he experienced a nosebleed, which took 30 minutes to stop by applying pressure. He has no history of exposure to any patients or epilepsy or any other seizure disorder. He is not taking any medication. Its temperature is 39.1 ° C (102.4 ° F), pulse 106 / min, respiration 26 / min, blood pressure 128/70 mmHg. He is confused and disoriented. Examination shows pallor and diffuse petechiae on the trunk and arms. The throat is soft, and neurological examination is otherwise within normal limits. Laboratory results: hemoglobin 9 g / dL; white blood cell count 8,200 / mm3; platelet count 34,000 / mm3; prothrombin time 13 seconds; partial thromboplastin time 30 seconds; fibrin split product negative; serum creatinine 2.9 mg / dL; bilirubin total 3.2 mg / dL, direct 0.4 mg / dL; lactate dehydrogenase 559 U / L. Peripheral blood smears show a lot of schistocytes. Which of the following is the best next step in management?
A. Electroencephalography
B. Packed red blood cell transfusion
C. CT scan of the head
D. Plasma exchange therapy
E. Fresh frozen plasma (FFP) transfusions
F. MRI scan of the head
G. Platelet transfusion
H. Intravenous tranexamic acid

A 67-year-old male came to the emergency department with two cases of red urine since this morning. There is no pain in urination. He complained of lower back pain and fever. He was diagnosed with right knee osteoarthritis six months ago and took 1 to 2 tablets of ibuprofen a day. He smoked a pack of cigarettes every day for the past 45 years. Don't drink alcohol. He has a temperature of 38.5 ° C, a pulse of 95 / min, and a blood pressure 130/80 mm Hg. Physical examination shows mild, diffuse maculopapular scarring and pain in the flank on both sides. The rest of the tests are normal. Urine analysis shows: Blood + 3 Protein + 1 RBC 10-12 hpf RBC Cast Negative high levels of eosinophils Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A. Acute tubulointerstitial nephritis
B. Acute pyelonephritis
C. Acute glomerulonephritis
D. Crystal-induced acute kidney injury
E. Carcinomas of kidney cells
F. Hench-Schonline Puerpura
G. Acute tubular necrosis

A 50-year-old male patient came to the doctor with complaints of problems due to erectile dysfunction during sexual intercourse over a 6-month period. He has type 2 diabetes mellitus which is well controlled with metformin. He doesn't smoke. He drinks 5 to 6 beers every day. His vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination shows bilateral leg swelling, decreased testis volume, and increased breast tissue. The spleen is palpable 2 cm below the left costal margin. Abdominal ultrasound shows atrophic, hyperechoic, nodular liver. An upper endoscopy is performed and the distal esophagus shows dilated submucosal veins of 2 mm diameter and red spots on their surface. He began therapy with sildenafil for erectile dysfunction. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in the management of the patient's esophageal findings?
A. Injection sclerotherapy
B. Nadolol therapy
C. Losaratan therapy
D. octreotide therapy
E. Isosorbide mononitrate therapy
F. Endoscopic band ligation
G. Transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt
H. Metoprolol therapy

A 45-year-old woman is visiting the doctor due to exhaustion and irregular menstrual cycles for the past year. He also complained of recurrent sinus infections. He has had frequent urination and swelling of the legs in the last six months. For three weeks, he has been struggling to lift his 3-year-old niece. He was recently diagnosed with depression. He worked as a medical assistant. The patient smoked a half-pack of cigarettes daily for 25 years and drank four beers on weekends. His only medication is escitalopram. He is 160 cm (5 ft 3 in) tall and weighs 79 kg (175 lb); BMI is 31 kg / m2. He looks tired. Temperature 37 ° C (98.6 ° F), pulse 80 / min, respiration 18 / min, blood pressure 140/82 mmHg. Physical examination reveals thickening of the throat and swelling of the abdomen. There are multiple injury marks on the skin on the arms and legs. There is general weakness and atrophy of the proximal muscles. The results of the laboratory: Serum Na + 150 mEq / L K + 3.0 mEq / L Cl-103 mEq / L HCO3 - 30 mEq / L Urea Nitrogen 19 mg / dL Creatinine 0.9 mg / dL Glucose 136 mg / dL A 1 mg overnight dexamethasone suppression test found serum cortisol 167 nmol / L (N < 50) and 24-hour urine cortisol 425 μg (N < 300 μg). Serum ACTH is 169 pg / mL (N = 7-50). A later high-dose dexamethasone suppression trial found serum cortisol levels of 164 nmol / L (N < 50). Which of the following is the most likely underlying cause of the patient's symptoms?
A. Extrinsic corticosteroid intake
B. Pituitary adenoma
C. Adrenal carcinoma
D. Hypothyroidism
E. Pheochromocytoma
F. small cell lung cancer
G. Adrenal adenoma

The 24-year-old first pregnant woman, at 38 weeks gestation, came to the doctor for a pre-natal visit. Transabdominal ultrasound at the last two pre-natal visits showed the baby in the breech position. She has no medical issues and only takes pre-natal vitamins. His pulse is 95 / min, breathing 16 / min, blood pressure 130/76 mm Hg. The abdomen is soft and insensitive; no contractions are felt. Pelvic examination shows cervical dehydration and uterine prolapse consistent with 38 weeks gestation. Fetal heart rate tracing shows a baseline heart rate of 152 / min and 2 accelerated increases at 10 min. Today's repeat ultrasound also showed a consistent breech position. The patient said she wanted to try a vaginal delivery. Which of the following is the best next management step?
A. Suggest a Caesarean section
B. Monitor up to automatic delivery
C. Repeat the ultrasound in a week.
D. Suggest an external head replacement (external cephalic version)
E. Suggest an internal Podalic version

A 4-year-old boy was brought to the emergency department with a fever, swallowing pains, headaches, and a tight neck that began shortly after waking up. He had a sore throat last week that escalated sharply this morning. He has no history of serious illness and does not take any medication. He lives with his mother. The elder brother has asthma. Vaccination is complete. The patient appears to be seriously ill. Temperature 38.4 ° C, pulse 95 / min, respiration 33 / min, blood pressure 93/60 mmHg. On examination, it is found that the saliva is leaking. The neck is stiff and the extension is limited. Auxiliary muscles are used for breathing. Inspiratory striders can be heard when listening to the chest. There are no abnormalities in the examination of the heart. Oropharyngeal examination shows a raised area in the posterior pharyngeal wall. Veins have been inserted and lab tests ordered. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in patient management?
A. Endotracheal intubation
B. Intravenous antibiotics
C. The Culture of Blood
D. Intravenous corticosteroids
E. CT scan of the neck
F. nebulized albuterol
G. X-ray of the lateral neck

An 8-year-old boy has been brought to the doctor because he has a history of a 7-day progressive cough. Coughing occurs in spells and there are approximately 5-10 coughs in a row. He takes deep, noisy breaths after each spell. Sometimes he vomits after coughing. He had a runny nose for a week before he started coughing. His vaccination records are not available. She lives in an apartment with her father, mother, and 2-week-old younger sister. The mother was given the Tdap vaccine 11 years ago. There is no vaccination record of the father. Its temperature is 37.8 ° C (100 ° F). No abnormalities were found in the test. Its leukocyte count is 42,000 / mm3. Throat swab culture and PCR results are awaited. Which of the following would be the most appropriate recommendation for this family?
A. Give oral azithromycin to the baby and father, and Tdap vaccination for the father.
B. Give oral erythromycin to the baby and father, and Tdap vaccination for the father.
C. Give oral azithromycin to all family members and Tdap vaccination for father and mother.
D. Give oral trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole to all family members and Tdap vaccination for the father.
E. Give oral trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole to all family members and Tdap vaccination for father and mother.
F. Give oral erythromycin to all family members and Tdap vaccination for father and mother.
G. Give oral erythromycin to all family members and Tdap vaccination for the father.
H. Give oral trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole for father and baby (baby) and Tdap vaccine for father.
I. Give oral azithromycin to all family members and Tdap vaccination for the father.

Police brought a 23-year-old male to the emergency department with cognitive impairment and agitation after he suffered a head injury at a local nightclub. The patient refuses to answer questions and is severely agitated. There is a smell of alcohol. His physical examination: temperature 36.9 ° C, pulse 104 / min, respiration 24 / min, blood pressure 148/95 mmHg. He is confused and only knows the person's name. The nerve test shows myosis and nystagmus but stops quickly if the patient tries to attack some of the care team. A CT scan of the head is normal. Is the ingestion of any of the following substances likely to be the cause of the patient's symptoms?
A. Heroin
B. Alcohol
C. cannabis
D. Cocaine
E. Gamma-hydroxybutyric acid
F. Lysergic acid diethylamide
G. Methamphetamine
H. Phensiclidine

A 34-year-old AIDS patient comes to the doctor because his right eye has been losing vision and showing dark spots for the past two days. There is no pain and the left eye is normal. He had been treated with fluconazole for fungal esophagitis six months earlier. He was diagnosed with Kaposi's sarcoma two years ago. Current medications include efavirenz, tenofovir, emtricitabine, azithromycin, trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, multivitamins, and a nutritional supplement. He is 170 cm (5 ft 7 in) tall and weighs 45 kg (99 lb); with a body mass index of 15.6 kg / m2. Temperature 37 ° C (98.6 ° F), pulse 89 / min, blood pressure 110/70 mmHg. Examination reveals cervical lymphadenopathy. He has multiple purple plaques on his trunk and limbs. Fundoscopy examination shows granular-whiteish yellow opacities around the retinal vessels and areas of multiple dot-blot hemorrhages. His CD4 + T-lymphocyte count is 36 / m3. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A. Cytomegalovirus retinitis
B. Herpes simplex keratitis
C. Toxoplasma retinitis
D. HIV retinopathy
E. Varicella Zoster Retinitis

A 65-year-old Asian woman visits the doctor for a routine health maintenance exam. During questioning, he reported occasional night sweats over the past two months, but no fever or weight loss. He had an acute myocardial infarction (heart attack) seven months earlier and received treatment with percutaneous coronary intervention. He has hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and gastroesophageal reflux disease. He smoked a pack of cigarettes every day for 37 years. Current medications include aspirin, atorvastatin, ramipril, metoprolol, and esomeprazole. He is 178 cm (5 ft 10 in) tall and weighs 89 kg (207 lb); BMI is 29.70 kg / m2. Temperature 37.4 ° C (99.3 ° F), pulse 84 / min, respiration 18 / min, and blood pressure 145/80 mmHg. Lung sounds are normal; S4 sounds are found in the heart. There is a non-painful skin lesion near the right big toe, the photo of which is displayed. The rest of the test shows no discrepancy. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A. Cholesterol embolism
B. Bleeding under the affected nail
C. Malignant melanoma
D. Onychomyces (fungal infection of the nails)
E. Squamous cell carcinoma

A 26-year-old African-American woman visits a patient at the doctor's because she has been experiencing an aproductive cough and chest pain in the past 4 days. The pain is sharp and increases with deep breathing. During this period, he developed hematuria (blood in the urine) twice. Over the past 6 months, he has had periodic pain, stiffness, and swelling between his finger and left knee. She has had two miscarriages, aged 22 and 24. Her only medication is minocycline for acne vulgaris. It has a temperature of 38.1 ° C (100.6 ° F), a pulse of 75 / min, and a blood pressure 138/85 mm Hg. A physical examination revealed a red rash on his face. Both metacarpophalangeal joints have mild sensitivity but no hot or redness. What is the most likely outcome from further evaluation of this patient?
A. Anti-histone antibodies
B. Low levels of serum C3 and C4
C. Increased bleeding time
D. Damage to the metacarpophalangeal joint
E. Bilateral enlargement of the hilar lymph node
F. Cytotoxic glomerular antibodies

A 5-month-old male baby has been brought to the doctor by his mother because he has had a generalized itchy rash for two weeks. The child wakes up at night because of the itching. She was exclusively breastfed until formula was switched to milk at 4 months of age. His father has a history of asthma. Vaccinations have been updated. Height in the 75th percentile and weight in the 70th percentile. Tests show dry and scaly patches of extensors on the face and limbs. Green is preserved. Which of the following is the best next management step?
A. Local Coal Tar
B. Oral acyclovir
C. Oral vitamin A
D. Local mupirocin
E. Local clotrimazole
F. Tarred shampoo
G. Local emollient

Two hours after having a left femoral artery embolectomy, a 63-year-old obese woman is suffering in her left leg with severe pain, numbness, and tingling sensations. The surgery was without complications and the parietal pulse was weakly palpable after the procedure. He has type 2 diabetes mellitus, peripheral artery disease, hypertension, and hypercholesterolemia. He was taking insulin, enalapril, carvedilol, aspirin, and rosuvastatin before being admitted. He looks uncomfortable. Temperature 37.1 ° C (99.3 ° F), pulse 98 / min, blood pressure 132/90 mm Hg. Examination shows surgical incision of the left groin; the left lower limb is swollen, stiff, and sensitive to touch. Dorsiflex causes severe pain in the calf. The femoral pulse is palpable on both sides, but the pedal pulse is weaker on the left than on the right. Lab results: hemoglobin 12.1 g / dL, white blood cells 11,300 / mm3, platelets 189,000 / mm3; serum glucose 222 mg / dL, creatinine 1.1 mg / dL; urinalysis normal. Which of the following is the most likely cause of these symptoms?
A. Deep vein thrombosis
B. Reperfusion injury
C. rhabdomyolysis
D. Cholesterol embolism
E. Cellulitis

A 17-year-old boy has been brought in to the doctor with right knee pain that has been growing slowly over the past three months. He reports that the pain is worse at night and when playing sports at school. There is no history of any knee injury or any previous joint problems. His vital signs are within normal limits. Examination of the right knee shows mild swelling and sensitivity, but no hotness or redness; movement is limited. He goes to the analgesic gate. Experimental blood results show alkaline phosphatase 180 u / l and erythrocyte sedimentation rate of 80 mm / h. Below is an X-ray of the right knee. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A. Osteoclastoma
B. Ewing sarcoma
C. Cordoma
D. Osteochondroma
E. Chondrosarcoma
F. Osteosarcoma

A 17-year-old girl has been brought to the doctor with four months of amenorrhea (no menstrual periods). Previously, her menses were regular, occurring every 28 days and lasting 3 to 4 days. There is no family history of serious illness. He gets good grades in school and participates on the high school track team. She is sexually active with a single male partner and regularly uses condoms. His physique looks lean. Examination shows an enlargement of the bilateral parotid gland. The body has fine fur. Blood test results: thyroid-stimulating hormone 3.7 μU / mL, prolactin 16 ng / mL, estradiol 23 pg / mL (normal > 40), follicle-stimulating hormone 1.6 mIU / mL, luteinizing hormone 2.8 mIU / mL. Urine pregnancy test is negative. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this outcome?
A. The use of external steroids
B. Defects in the androgen receptor
C. Gonadal dysgenesis
D. Abnormal migration of nerve cells
E. Hyperandrogenic anovulation
F. Nutritional deficiencies

The 21-year-old college student came to the doctor with intermittent palpitations (heart rhythm abnormalities). He has no chest pain or shortness of breath. The symptoms began two days ago, when he returned to the dormitory after a four-hour bus ride from home. The day before, he had gone to a party with friends. Since then, palpitations have increased and become more frequent. The patient smoked five cigarettes per day for the past three years. He drinks four to six glasses of alcohol with friends once or twice a week and occasionally uses marijuana. She is sexually active with a boyfriend and is taking oral contraceptives. He doesn't look worried. Its pulse is 100 per minute, irregular; blood pressure 140/85 mm Hg; respiration is 25 per minute. Physical examination reveals subtle tremors in both hands, hot limbs, and swollen lower legs. The respiratory tract is clear when listening. Below is the ECG (electrocardiogram). Which of the following is the most appropriate next management step?
A. Measure T-S-H (thyroid stimulating hormone) levels
B. Watch and wait
C. Give intravenous adenosine
D. Measure the D-dimer level
E. Give subcutaneous (under the skin) enoxaparin.
F. send urine toxicology test

A 20-year-old college student has come to the doctor because he has been extremely sad and constantly crying for the past three weeks. Three weeks ago, her boyfriend left her after a four-year relationship. He has no appetite and has lost 2.3 kg (5.1 lb). She missed a few classes because she couldn't stop crying or get out of bed. She always thinks about her ex-boyfriend. She says she experienced similar symptoms for about two months, even after the previous relationship ended. The patient is 158 cm (5 ft 2 in) tall and weighs 45 kg (100 lb); BMI is 18 kg / m2. Its temperature is 36.1 ° C (97 ° F), pulse 65 / min, blood pressure 110/60 mm Hg. A physical examination revealed no abnormalities. Psychiatric tests show he is sad and cries easily. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A. Borderline personality disorder
B. sad state of affairs
C. Adjustment disorder with depressive mood
D. Chronic depressive disorder
E. Severe depressive disorder
F. Sudden Stress Disorder
G. anorexia nervosa

A 16-year-old girl is brought to the doctor because her mother is concerned about her anorexia and lack of weight gain. He has lost 7 kg (15 lb) in the last 3 months. The patient says he needs to lose more weight because he doesn't want to be overweight anymore. She keeps a diary of her daily calorie intake. Menarch was 13 years old, and the last menstrual period was 3 months ago. He participated on the high school track team. She is sexually active with two male partners and uses condoms infrequently. Her height is in the 50th percentile and her weight and BMI are below the 5th percentile. He has a temperature of 37 ° C (98.6 ° F), a pulse of 58 / min, and a blood pressure 96/60 mm Hg. Examination reveals fine fur on the trunk and limbs. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A. HIV infection
B. Disorders related to deformities of the body
C. Bulimia nervosa
D. Type 1 diabetes mellitus
E. Hyperthyroidism
F. Obsessive-compulsive disorder
G. anorexia nervosa

A 27-year-old woman came to the emergency department because of increasing insensitivity and weakness in her left arm and left leg over the past two days. He is also experiencing a strong urge to urinate and incessant urination during this period. Three months ago, he had blurred vision, difficulty distinguishing colors, and headaches for a week, which have now healed. The patient smoked a half-pack of cigarettes every day for 10 years and drank four glasses of wine each week. Its temperature is 37 ° C (98.6 ° F), pulse 78 / min, respiration 14 / min, blood pressure 110/68 mm Hg. The test shows 3 / 5 strength in the left arm and leg and 5 / 5 in the right side. While bending the neck, the patient feels a lightning shot going down along his spine. MRIs of the brain show gadolinium-enhancing lesions in the right central sulcus, cervical spinal cord, and optic nerve. Which of the following is the best next step in the management of this patient?
A. Dimethyl fumarate therapy
B. Interferon beta therapy
C. Give Lorazepam
D. IV Give methylprednisolone
E. Plasmapheresis
F. Provide tissue plasminogen activator
G. Glatiramer acetate therapy

A 35-year-old male was brought to the emergency department after a car accident. The patient was on his way to work when he lost control of the car and hit a tree. On arrival, the patient appears weak and lethargic, with abdominal pain. Its temperature is 37 ° C (98.6 ° F), pulse 121 / min, respiration 22 / min, blood pressure 85/60 mm Hg. He is conscious of the individual but not of space or time. There are no abnormal sounds in the lungs; cardiac examination shows tachycardia but no murmur, rubbing, or gallops. The abdominal examination consists of a few bruises above the navel and a wide range of sensitivities. Focused ultrasound (FAST) of the trauma has been performed but the results are uncertain. In addition to vein-based fluid resuscitation, which of the following is the best next step in the management of this patient?
A. Angiography and embolization
B. CT scan of the abdomen
C. exploratory laparotomy
D. insertion of the nasogastric tube
E. Abdominal X-ray
F. Diagnostic peritoneal lavage

A 24-year-old male, who has been experiencing chronic back pain, visits a physician for care after relocating to Florida. He complained of anxiety, nausea, abdominal cramping, vomiting, and diarrhea for three days. He said not to smoke, drink and use illegal drugs. He looks restless. It has a temperature of 37 ° C (98.6 ° F), a pulse of 110 / min, and a blood pressure 150/86 mm Hg. Physical examination shows enlarged pupils, sweating, and hair loss. Abdominal examination shows extensive light sensitivity; no rebound tenderness or guarding. He has a hemoglobin of 14.5 g / dL, a white blood cell count of 8,000 / mm3, and a platelet count of 250,000 / mm3; serum tests and urinalysis show no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most appropriate pharmacotherapy?
A. Lorazepam
B. Naltrexone
C. Methadone
D. Morphine
E. Naloxone

A 38-year-old woman visits the doctor for a follow-up visit. He has two years of chronic depressed mood and fatigue, which is associated with waking up early in the morning. A week ago, he started to need less sleep and now feels rested after about 5 hours of sleep a night. Two similar episodes occurred six months and a year ago. He reported increased energy and sexual desire. He lost 4kg (8.8lb) in the last month. She does not feel the need for food and says her energy comes "from the world." She enjoyed working as a librarian. He started taking fluoxetine three months ago. In psychic tests, he is alert and aware of time and space; but irritable. There is no audible or visible hallucination. Physical examination is normal. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A. Drug-induced bipolar disorder
B. Bipolar disorder with rapid cycling
C. Mayabic disorder
D. Schizoaffective disorder
E. Cyclothymic disorder

A 45-year-old woman came to the doctor complaining of fatigue and excessive thirst for two weeks. During this period, he is unable to sleep through the night due to frequent urge to urinate. He also urinates more often than usual during the day. He drinks 4 to 5 litres of water and 1 to 2 beers every day. He has autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease, hypertension controlled with lisinopril, and bipolar disorder. Valproic acid therapy was started three months ago after a manic episode. Biological signs are within normal limits. Irregular flank knots are found on both flanks. The rest of the physical exam shows no abnormalities. The results of the laboratory: Serum Na + 152 mEq / L K + 4.1 mEq / L Cl - 100 mEq / L HCO3 - 25 mEq / L Creatinine 1.8 mg / dL Asymmetry 312 mOsmol / kg Glucose 98 mg / dL Urinary incontinence of 190 mOsmol / kg Urinary incontinence does not change after 3 hours, even when no fluid is taken or desmopressin is given. Which of the following is the best next step for management?
A. metformin therapy
B. Additional water restrictions
C. Amiloride therapy

A 43-year-old woman came to the doctor because she had a painless ulcer on the bottom of her right foot for 3 months. There is no history of injury. He cleans the ulcer once daily with gauze at home.
